The `get_approaching_overtime` tool returns a nested JSON structure accessible via `json.loads(raw[0]['text'])` when reading from stored tool results; the employees array contains `status` values of `ok`, `watch`, `in_danger`, and `overtime`, with `actualHours`, `remainingHours`, `projectedHours`, `projectedOtHours`, and `projectedOtCost` fields per employee. Region IDs are stable UUIDs \u2014 Cincinnati's is `26d3c550-c573-4b82-bae6-09887cf0fd49`, Toledo's is `2467c273-eaf6-4f47-8e25-388a5466b52c`.</chat>\n\n<chat url=\"https://claude.ai/chat/099fa57a-f04e-41e6-8b73-7b18744005e1\" updated_at=\"2026-09-01T17:34:05.568882+00:00\" kind=\"summary\">Title: Building an AI bot for workforce management automation\nBuilding an AI bot for workforce management automation\n&lt;chat_summary&gt;**Conversation overview**\n\nThe person is building an AI-powered admin automation system for Chronotek, their Workforce Management SaaS product (referred to as \"Chronotek Next\" for the current version under development). Everything was packaged as a ready-to-unpack git repo zip with a `docs/KICKOFF_PROMPT.md` for initiating the Claude Code session. All schemas and fixtures were validated programmatically before delivery (11/11 positive fixtures passing; four negative cases correctly rejected).\n\nKey architectural decisions recorded as settled: TypeScript MCP SDK with streamable HTTP transport; `ct_admin_{entity}_{action}` naming convention matching the existing `ct_analyze_*` analytics tools (which are explicitly out of scope for this server); three interaction patterns (paired options-then-write, simple write, two-phase destructive confirm); server-side revalidation as non-negotiable on every write; composite server-side endpoints owning full transaction sagas; `optionsToken` for staleness detection; one UUID `idempotencyKey` per user intent for idempotency; structured error results (never protocol errors) with `validValues` teaching recovery. Real-data lessons encoded explicitly: the duplicate-employee guard on name and phone at hire time, and the `*Any Employee` placeholder record pattern meaning unfilled open shifts, not assignable people. The person confirmed MCP is the preferred interface for pluggability reasons and wants to move implementation to Claude Code. The conversation closed with the handoff package delivered and the sequencing rationale explained: build the framework skeleton around the shipped schedule pair first, enumerate the rest at catalog level only, and write full specs per family just-in-time as each phase begins.</chat>\n\n<chat url=\"https://claude.ai/chat/0d75d822-d477-4f57-9b7f-5c87030b44cc\" updated_at=\"2026-07-03T11:03:39.563017+00:00\" kind=\"summary\">Title: Optimizing janitorial operations with MCP data analysis\nOptimizing janitorial operations with MCP data analysis\nThe person demonstrated a preference for pragmatic staging: validate the concept manually before committing to infrastructure, and make deliberate tool choices that reduce rework later.\n\n**Tool knowledge**\n\nThe CAP - MCP server is a remote HTTP server already hosted on Replit. Claude Code connects to remote MCP servers using `claude mcp add --transport http` followed by the server name and URL, with OAuth authentication completed inside the session via the `/mcp` command for servers requiring sign-in. A noteworthy configuration detail: Claude Code emits warnings when MCP tool output exceeds 10,000 tokens, and this limit can be raised via the `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` environment variable, which matters for this use case if rollup or summary tools return large payloads. The CAP - MCP tools confirmed to exist include overtime data (actuals and predictive), timecard infractions, job time by customer and by job, and employee travel \u2014 though the exact tool names, parameters, and return shapes are intended to be discovered experimentally during the first analysis run rather than assumed in advance.&lt;/chat_summary&gt;</chat>\n\n<chat url=\"https://claude.ai/chat/1977a088-2e89-491c-bb39-a2ce82bd7657\" updated_at=\"2026-09-16T21:13:18.713076+00:00\" kind=\"summary\">Title: Multi-model AI group chat setup\nMulti-model AI group chat setup\n&lt;chat_summary&gt;**Conversation Overview**\n\nThe person asked how to create a mixed AI group chat combining instances of Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. Claude built a complete local orchestration application called \"Roundtable\" that puts the person and multiple AI participants from both providers into a shared room with a unified transcript.\n\nClaude designed and delivered a full working application consisting of a core Python orchestrator (`roundtable.py`), a single-file web UI (`index.html`), a comprehensive test suite (`test_roundtable.py`), supporting configuration files (`config.example.json`, `.env.example`, `requirements.txt`), a Windows launcher (`run.bat`), and a `README.md`. The architecture uses sequential turn-taking so each AI sees prior replies before responding, a shared `Transcript` class, and separate provider adapter classes for Anthropic's Messages API and OpenAI's Responses API. Key features include `@Name` mention routing, `/go N` autonomous rounds, `PASS` token for opting out, graceful error handling per participant, and context trimming at ~60k characters. Both a terminal CLI mode and a local web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:8765` are supported. The default roster is four participants: Fable-1, Astra-1, Fable-2, Astra-2, each with distinct personas. The company reports up to 200x faster inference and 400x lower cost than comparable LLMs on classification tasks. This post covers how Jev works, where it fits into the agent loop, and how to use it with LangChain. Jev is actually not a traditional LLM, it doesn\u2019t generate text. It\u2019s trained using reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions (RLCD). \n\nYour code uses those results to guide what an agent does next, without a full chat LLM call for each decision. To invoke a Jev model, you send it a state (the context) and questions about that state.\n\nThat makes it straightforward to call Jev from a node or middleware hook using the context your agent already has.         "text": "Jev is a small component inside a regular application, added where code needs one judgment. It comes from TypeSafe AI, a San Francisco lab that came out of stealth on September 15, 2026 with $40M in seed funding and Jev as its first public model.\n\nWith ChatGPT or a coding agent, the AI is the interface or the worker. Jev is a small component inside a regular application, added where code needs one judgment. It comes from TypeSafe AI, a San Francisco lab that came out of stealth on September 15, 2026 with $40M in seed funding and Jev as its first public model. TypeSafe calls it a System One model: built to make fast decisions inside software, not to chat with people. This post covers what Jev is, how you call it, how to write questions for it, where it fails, and where I would put it in my own projects. The simplest way to describe it: Jev is a smart if statement. Ordinary code branches on values it can compute, like if (order.total > 100). \n\nIf this works, the major providers have a reason to ship decision models of their own.\n\nComposing AI into software is not new. Developers do it with small LLMs, embeddings, classifiers, and structured outputs. Jev\u2019s contribution is a model and API designed only for that role: low latency, low cost, typed answers, probabilities as the normal output. Before Jev, we had three common ways to make this kind of decision in software: Write an if, a regular expression, or a decision tree. Train a classifier for a specific set of labels. Ask a general-purpose LLM to return structured output. Rules are fast, cheap, and predictable, but brittle when meaning matters. A classifier is fast too, but needs labeled examples, a training step, and a separate model per task. A general-purpose LLM understands unstructured text with no per-task training, but it is still a generative model, even when you constrain its answer to JSON. Jev aims for the middle.",

    "start_timestamp": "2026-09-23T02:21:22.782282Z",
    "stop_timestamp": "2026-09-23T02:21:22.792994Z",
    "flags": null,
    "type": "text",
    "text": "Yes, but not in the way \"learn\" usually means for game-playing AI. Jev is a pretrained decision model, not an agent you train on a game. To invoke a Jev model, you send it a state (the context) and questions about that state, and it takes an input and returns one of three output types: a yes/no answer with a confidence score, a category pick from a defined list, or a numeric score on a scale.\n\nSo Pac-Man works like this: you write a harness that serializes each frame's state (Pac-Man's position, ghost positions and modes, remaining pellets, walls) as text, then ask \"Which direction: up/down/left/right?\" and act on the answer. That's exactly what its launch demos did \u2014 early demos focus on real-time control, including a Minecraft bot, a self-driving style simulation, a Subway Surfers style game, and a simulated drone navigating an obstacle course, and it also plays Doom. Pac-Man is arguably easier than several of those, and the latency fits a game loop: it answers all of them in one parallel pass in 70 to 500 milliseconds.\n\nThe key difference from classic RL game agents (like DeepMind's Atari work): Jev doesn't improve by playing. It has no online learning \u2014 it applies general judgment to whatever state description you feed it, zero-shot, from the first frame. Its skill ceiling is set by how well you describe the state and frame the questions, not by hours of gameplay. It also doesn't see pixels; you have to hand it structured state. So \"just a machine learning system\" is fair, but it's closer to a smart, fast conditional in your code than to a learning agent.",

  {
    "start_timestamp": "2026-09-23T02:23:23.562679Z",
    "stop_timestamp": "2026-09-23T02:23:30.534886Z",
    "flags": null,
    "type": "text",
    "text": "Yes \u2014 that's the whole point of it. Jev ships pretrained; there's no per-task training step. You give it the game state and a question, and it answers on the first frame it ever sees. That's how the Doom, Minecraft, and Subway Surfers demos worked, and those were built fast and cheap without game-specific training.\n\nTwo caveats on what \"no prior training\" buys you:\n\n1. **You still have to build the harness.** Jev doesn't see the screen or press buttons. Someone writes code that reads the game's state (positions, ghost modes, pellets, walls), turns it into text, asks \"which direction?\", and feeds the answer back as a keypress. That's an afternoon of engineering, not training, but it isn't zero work.\n\n2. **It won't get better over time.** Since it isn't learning from play, its performance on frame 10,000 is the same as frame 1. If it plays badly, the fix is rewriting how you describe the state or what you ask \u2014 not more reps. Compare that to a DQN-style agent, which starts at random and improves, but needs millions of frames to get there.\n\nSo: competent Pac-Man out of the box, plausible; superhuman Pac-Man through practice, no \u2014 that's not what it does.",
    "citations": []
  }
]

      "file_text": "\"\"\"Maze layouts.\n\nLegend\n------\n``#``  wall\n``.``  pellet\n``o``  power pellet\n``P``  player start (exactly one)\n``G``  ghost spawn (one or more; ghosts cycle through them)\n`` ``  empty corridor (walkable, no pellet)\n\nLayouts are original designs for a Pac-Man-style pellet/ghost game. Every\nlayout is validated on import: rectangular, fully enclosed by walls, exactly\none ``P``, at least one ``G``, and every pellet/ghost cell reachable from ``P``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections import deque\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nWALL, PELLET, POWER, PLAYER, GHOST, EMPTY = \"#\", \".\", \"o\", \"P\", \"G\", \" \"\nVALID_CHARS = {WALL, PELLET, POWER, PLAYER, GHOST, EMPTY}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Layout:\n    name: str\n    walls: np.ndarray  # bool (H, W)\n    pellets: np.ndarray  # bool (H, W) regular pellets\n    powers: np.ndarray  # bool (H, W) power pellets\n    player_start: tuple[int, int]\n    ghost_starts: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]\n\n    @property\n    def height(self) -> int:\n        return int(self.walls.shape[0])\n\n    @property\n    def width(self) -> int:\n        return int(self.walls.shape[1])\n\n    @property\n    def n_pellets(self) -> int:\n        return int(self.pellets.sum() + self.powers.sum())\n\n\ndef parse_layout(name: str, text: str) -> Layout:\n    rows = [r for r in text.strip(\"\\n\").split(\"\\n\")]\n    if not rows:\n        raise ValueError(f\"{name}: empty layout\")\n    width = len(rows[0])\n    if any(len(r) != width for r in rows):\n        raise ValueError(f\"{name}: all rows must have the same width\")\n    height = len(rows)\n\n    walls = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=bool)\n    pellets = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=bool)\n    powers = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=bool)\n    player: tuple[int, int] | None = None\n    ghosts: list[tuple[int, int]] = []\n\n    for y, row in enumerate(rows):\n        for x, ch in enumerate(row):\n            if ch not in VALID_CHARS:\n                raise ValueError(f\"{name}: invalid char {ch!r} at ({y},{x})\")\n            if ch == WALL:\n                walls[y, x] = True\n            elif ch == PELLET:\n                pellets[y, x] = True\n            elif ch == POWER:\n                powers[y, x] = True\n            elif ch == PLAYER:\n                if player is not None:\n                    raise ValueError(f\"{name}: more than one player start\")\n                player = (y, x)\n            elif ch == GHOST:\n                ghosts.append((y, x))\n\n    if player is None:\n        raise ValueError(f\"{name}: no player start 'P'\")\n    if not ghosts:\n        raise ValueError(f\"{name}: no ghost spawn 'G'\")\n    border = np.concatenate([walls[0], walls[-1], walls[:, 0], walls[:, -1]])\n    if not border.all():\n        raise ValueError(f\"{name}: layout must be enclosed by walls\")\n\n    layout = Layout(name, walls, pellets, powers, player, tuple(ghosts))\n    unreachable = _unreachable_targets(layout)\n    if unreachable:\n        raise ValueError(f\"{name}: unreachable cells from player start: {unreachable[:5]}\")\n    return layout\n\n\ndef reachable_from(walls: np.ndarray, start: tuple[int, int]) -> deque[tuple[int, int]] = deque([start])\n    while q:\n        y, x = q.popleft()\n        for dy, dx in ((-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)):\n            ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx\n            if 0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and not walls[ny, nx] and not seen[ny, nx]:\n                seen[ny, nx] = True\n                q.append((ny, nx))\n    return seen\n\n\ndef _unreachable_targets(layout: True\n    bad = np.argwhere(targets & ~seen)\n    return [tuple(int(v) for v in p) for p in bad]\n\n\nSMALL = dict[str, Layout] = {\n    \"small\": parse_layout(\"small\", SMALL),\n    \"medium\": parse_layout(\"medium\", MEDIUM),\n}\n\n\ndef get_layout(name: str) -> Layout:\n    try:\n        return Fully deterministic given a seed.\n\nObservation: ``float32`` tensor of shape ``(NUM_CHANNELS, H, W)``:\n\n=====  ===============================================\nindex  channel\n=====  ===============================================\n0      walls\n1      pellets\n2      power pellets\n3      player\n4      ghosts (dangerous)\n5      ghosts (frightened / edible)\n6      ghosts' previous positions (encodes heading)\n7      power timer fraction (uniform fill, 0..1)\n=====  ===============================================\n\nActions: 0 = up, 1 = down, 2 = left, 3 = right. Moving into a wall leaves the\nplayer in place (the step still counts and ghosts still move).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections import deque\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom .mazes import Layout, get_layout\n\nNUM_CHANNELS = 8\nACTIONS: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...] = ((-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1))\nACTION_NAMES = (\"up\", \"down\", \"left\", \"right\")\nN_ACTIONS = len(ACTIONS)\n_OPPOSITE = {0: 1, 1: 0, 2: 3, 3: 2}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Rewards:\n    \"\"\"Reward table, in game points.\"\"\"\n\n    pellet: float = 10.0\n    power: float = 50.0\n    ghost: float = 200.0\n    clear: float = 500.0\n    death: float = -500.0\n    step: float = -1.0\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass EnvConfig:\n    maze: str = \"small\"\n    n_ghosts: int = 1\n    lives: int = 1\n    max_steps: int = 500\n    power_duration: int = 20\n    ghost_respawn: int = 10\n    ghost_speed: float = 1.0\n    frightened_speed: float = 0.5\n    # Probability that ghost i chases (vs. moves randomly). Cycled if fewer than n_ghosts.\n    ghost_aggression: tuple[float, ...] = (0.9, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3)\n    rewards: Rewards = field(default_factory=Rewards)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Ghost:\n    home: tuple[int, int]\n    aggression: float\n    pos: tuple[int, int]\n    prev: tuple[int, int]\n    direction: int | None = None\n    respawn_in: int = 0  # >0 means eaten and waiting off-board\n\n    @property\n    def active(self) -> bool:\n        return self.respawn_in == 0\n\n\nclass MazeEnv:\n    metadata = {\"render_modes\": [\"ansi\"]}\n\n    def __init__(self, config: EnvConfig | None = None, **overrides):\n        cfg = config or EnvConfig()\n        for k, v in overrides.items():\n            if not hasattr(cfg, k):\n                raise TypeError(f\"unknown EnvConfig field {k!r}\")\n            setattr(cfg, k, v)\n        if cfg.n_ghosts < 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"n_ghosts must be >= 0\")\n        self.cfg = cfg\n        self.layout: Layout = get_layout(cfg.maze)\n        self.walls = self.layout.walls\n        self.height, self.width = self.walls.shape\n        self.observation_shape = (NUM_CHANNELS, self.height, self.width)\n        self.n_actions = N_ACTIONS\n        self._rng = np.random.default_rng()\n        self._dist_cache: dict[tuple[int, int], np.ndarray] = {}\n        self._reset_state()\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ API\n    def reset(self, seed: int | None = None, options=None):\n        if seed is not None:\n            self._rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n        self._reset_state()\n        return self._obs(), self._info()\n\n    def step(self, action: int):\n        if self.done:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"step() called on a finished episode; call reset()\")\n        action = int(action)\n        if not 0 <= action < N_ACTIONS:\n            raise ValueError(f\"invalid action {action}\")\n        R = self.cfg.rewards\n        reward = R.step\n        self.steps += 1\n        self.ghosts_eaten_this_step = 0\n\n        # --- player moves\n        dy, dx = ACTIONS[action]\n        ny, nx = self.player[0] + dy, self.player[1] + dx\n        if not self.walls[ny, nx]:\n            self.player = (ny, nx)\n\n        # --- eat\n        if self.pellets[self.player]:\n            self.pellets[self.player] = False\n            reward += R.pellet\n            self.score += R.pellet\n        elif self.powers[self.player]:\n            self.powers[self.player] = False\n            reward += R.power\n            self.score += R.power\n            self.power_timer = self.cfg.power_duration\n            for g in self.ghosts:\n                if g.active:\n                    g.direction = _OPPOSITE.get(g.direction, g.direction)\n\n        # --- collisions after player move\n        reward += self._resolve_collisions()\n        if not self.done:\n            # --- ghosts move\n            self._move_ghosts()\n            reward += self._resolve_collisions()\n\n        if self.power_timer > 0:\n            self.power_timer -= 1\n\n        terminated = False\n        truncated = False\n        if self.done:  # killed with no lives left\n            terminated = True\n        elif self.pellets_left == 0:\n            reward += R.clear\n            self.score += R.clear\n            self.won = True\n            self.done = True\n            terminated = True\n        elif self.steps >= self.cfg.max_steps:\n            truncated = True\n            self.done = True\n\n        return self._obs(), float(reward), terminated, truncated, self._info()\n\n    def render(self) -> str:\n        grid = np.where(self.walls, \"#\", \" \").astype(object)\n        grid[self.pellets] = \".\"\n        grid[self.powers] = \"o\"\n        for g in self.ghosts:\n            if g.active:\n                grid[g.pos] = \"g\" if self.power_timer > 0 else \"G\"\n        grid[self.player] = \"P\"\n        rows = [\"\".join(r) for r in grid]\n        status = f\"score={self.score:.0f} pellets_left={self.pellets_left} steps={self.steps} lives={self.lives}\"\n        return \"\\n\".join(rows + [status])\n\n    def legal_actions(self) -> list[int]:\n        return [a for a, (dy, dx) in enumerate(ACTIONS) if not self.walls[self.player[0] + dy, self.player[1] + dx]]\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------- internals\n    @property\n    def pellets_left(self) -> int:\n        return int(self.pellets.sum() + self.powers.sum())\n\n    def _reset_state(self) -> None:\n        self.pellets = self.layout.pellets.copy()\n        self.powers = self.layout.powers.copy()\n        self.lives = self.cfg.lives\n        self.score = 0.0\n        self.steps = 0\n        self.power_timer = 0\n        self.done = False\n        self.won = False\n        self.ghosts_eaten_this_step = 0\n        self._place_actors()\n\n    def _place_actors(self) -> None:\n        self.player = self.layout.player_start\n        homes = self.layout.ghost_starts\n        aggr = self.cfg.ghost_aggression\n        self.ghosts = [\n            Ghost(home=homes[i % len(homes)], aggression=aggr[i % len(aggr)], pos=homes[i % len(homes)], prev=homes[i % len(homes)])\n            for i in range(self.cfg.n_ghosts)\n        ]\n\n    def _resolve_collisions(self) -> float:\n        reward = 0.0\n        R = self.cfg.rewards\n        for g in self.ghosts:\n            if not g.active or g.pos != self.player:\n                continue\n            if self.power_timer > 0:\n                reward += R.ghost\n                self.score += R.ghost\n                self.ghosts_eaten_this_step += 1\n                g.respawn_in = self.cfg.ghost_respawn\n                g.pos = g.prev = g.home\n                g.direction = None\n            else:\n                reward += R.death\n                self.score += R.death\n                self.lives -= 1\n                if self.lives <= 0:\n                    self.done = True\n                else:\n                    self._place_actors()\n                    self.power_timer = 0\n                break\n        return reward\n\n    def _move_ghosts(self) -> None:\n        frightened = self.power_timer > 0\n        for g in self.ghosts:\n            if not g.active:\n                g.respawn_in -= 1\n                if g.respawn_in == 0:\n                    g.pos = g.prev = g.home\n                continue\n            speed = self.cfg.frightened_speed if frightened else self.cfg.ghost_speed\n            g.prev = g.pos\n            if self._rng.random() >= speed:\n                continue\n            legal = self._ghost_legal_moves(g)\n            if not legal:\n                continue\n            if self._rng.random() < g.aggression:\n                dist = self._distances(self.player)\n                scored = [(dist[g.pos[0] + ACTIONS[a][0], g.pos[1] + ACTIONS[a][1]], a) for a in legal]\n                best = min(scored)[0] if not frightened else max(scored)[0]\n                choices = [a for d, a in scored if d == best]\n                a = int(self._rng.choice(choices))\n            else:\n                a = int(self._rng.choice(legal))\n            g.direction = a\n            g.pos = (g.pos[0] + ACTIONS[a][0], g.pos[1] + ACTIONS[a][1])\n\n    def _ghost_legal_moves(self, g: Ghost) -> list[int]:\n        legal = [a for a, (dy, dx) in enumerate(ACTIONS) if not self.walls[g.pos[0] + dy, g.pos[1] + dx]]\n        if g.direction is not None and len(legal) > 1:\n            rev = _OPPOSITE[g.direction]\n            no_reverse = [a for a in legal if a != rev]\n            if no_reverse:\n                legal = no_reverse\n        return legal\n\n    def _distances(self, target: tuple[int, int]) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"BFS distance from every cell to ``target`` (cached per target).\"\"\"\n        cached = self._dist_cache.get(target)\n        if cached is not None:\n            return cached\n        dist = np.full(self.walls.shape, np.iinfo(np.int32).max // 2, dtype=np.int32)\n        dist[target] = 0\n        q: deque[tuple[int, int]] = deque([target])\n        while q:\n            y, x = q.popleft()\n            for dy, dx in ACTIONS:\n                ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx\n                if not self.walls[ny, nx] and dist[ny, nx] > dist[y, x] + 1:\n                    dist[ny, nx] = dist[y, x] + 1\n                    q.append((ny, nx))\n        self._dist_cache[target] = dist\n        return dist\n\n    def _obs(self) -> np.ndarray:\n        obs = np.zeros(self.observation_shape, dtype=np.float32)\n        obs[0] = self.walls\n        obs[1] = self.pellets\n        obs[2] = self.powers\n        obs[3][self.player] = 1.0\n        frightened = self.power_timer > 0\n        for g in self.ghosts:\n            if g.active:\n                obs[5 if frightened else 4][g.pos] = 1.0\n                obs[6][g.prev] = 1.0\n        if self.cfg.power_duration > 0:\n            obs[7] = self.power_timer / self.cfg.power_duration\n        return obs\n\n    def _info(self) -> dict:\n        return {\n            \"score\": self.score,\n            \"pellets_left\": self.pellets_left,\n            \"steps\": self.steps,\n            \"lives\": self.lives,\n            \"won\": self.won,\n            \"power_timer\": self.power_timer,\n            \"ghosts_eaten\": self.ghosts_eaten_this_step,\n        }\n\n\ndef make_gym_env(config: EnvConfig | None = None, **overrides):\n    \"\"\"Wrap :class:`MazeEnv` as a real ``gymnasium.Env`` if gymnasium is installed.\"\"\"\n    import gymnasium as gym  # optional dependency\n\n    class GymMazeEnv(gym.Env):\n        metadata = MazeEnv.metadata\n\n        def __init__(self):\n            super().__init__()\n            self.env = MazeEnv(config, **overrides)\n            self.observation_space = gym.spaces.Box(0.0, 1.0, self.env.observation_shape, np.float32)\n            self.action_space = gym.spaces.Discrete(N_ACTIONS)\n\n        def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):\n            super().reset(seed=seed)\n            return self.env.reset(seed=seed)\n\n        def step(self, action):\n            return self.env.step(action)\n\n        def render(self):\n            return self.env.render()\n\n    return GymMazeEnv()\n"

grid[self.pellets] = \".\"\n        grid[self.powers] = \"o\"\n        for g in self.ghosts:\n            if g.active:\n                grid[g.pos] = \"g\" if self.power_timer > 0 else \"G\"\n        grid[self.player] = \"P\"\n        rows = [\"\".join(r) for r in grid]\n        status = f\"score={self.score:.0f} pellets_left={self.pellets_left} steps={self.steps} lives={self.lives}\"\n        return \"\\n\".join(rows + [status])\n\n    def legal_actions(self) -> list[int]:\n        return [a for a, (dy, dx) in enumerate(ACTIONS) if not self.walls[self.player[0] + dy, self.player[1] +    def _reset_state(self) -> None:\n        self.pellets = self.layout.pellets.copy()\n        self.powers = self.layout.powers.copy()\n        self.lives = self.cfg.lives\n        self.score = 0.0\n        self.steps = 0\n        self.power_timer = 0\n        self.done = False\n        self.won = False\n        self.ghosts_eaten_this_step = 0\n        self._place_actors()\n\n    def _place_actors(self) -> None:\n        self.player = self.layout.player_start\n        homes = self.layout.ghost_starts\n        aggr = self.cfg.ghost_aggression\n        self.ghosts = [\n            Ghost(home=homes[i % len(homes)], aggression=aggr[i % len(aggr)], pos=homes[i % len(homes)], prev=homes[i % len(homes)])\n            for i in range(self.cfg.n_ghosts)\n        ]\n\n    def _resolve_collisions(self) -> float:\n        reward = 0.0\n        R = self.cfg.rewards\n        for g in self.ghosts:\n            if not g.active or g.pos != self.player:\n                continue\n            if self.power_timer > 0:\n                reward += R.ghost\n                self.score += R.ghost\n                self.ghosts_eaten_this_step += 1\n                g.respawn_in = self.cfg.ghost_respawn\n                g.pos = g.prev = g.home\n                g.direction = None\n            else:\n                reward += R.death\n                self.score += R.death\n                self.lives -= 1\n                if self.lives <= 0:\n                    self.done = True\n                else:\n                    self._place_actors()\n                    self.power_timer = 0\n                break\n        return reward\n\n    def _move_ghosts(self) -> None:\n        frightened = self.power_timer > 0\n        for g in self.ghosts:\n            if not g.active:\n                g.respawn_in -= 1\n                if g.respawn_in == 0:\n                    g.pos = g.prev = g.home\n                continue\n            speed = self.cfg.frightened_speed if frightened else self.cfg.ghost_speed\n            g.prev = g.pos\n            if self._rng.random() >= speed:\n                continue\n            legal = self._ghost_legal_moves(g)\n            if not legal:\n                continue\n            if self._rng.random() < g.aggression:\n                dist = self._distances(self.player)\n                scored = [(dist[g.pos[0] + ACTIONS[a][0], g.pos[1] + ACTIONS[a][1]], a) for a in legal]\n                best = min(scored)[0] if not frightened else max(scored)[0]\n                choices = [a for d, a in scored if d == best]\n                a = int(self._rng.choice(choices))\n            else:\n                a = int(self._rng.choice(legal))\n            g.direction = a\n            g.pos = (g.pos[0] + ACTIONS[a][0], g.pos[1] + ACTIONS[a][1])\n\n    def _ghost_legal_moves(self, g: Ghost) -> list[int]:\n        legal = [a for a, (dy, dx) in enumerate(ACTIONS) if not self.walls[g.pos[0] + dy, g.pos[1] + dx]]\n        if g.direction is not None and len(legal) > 1:\n            rev = _OPPOSITE[g.direction]\n            no_reverse = [a for a in legal if a != rev]\n            if no_reverse:\n                legal = no_reverse\n        return legal\n\n    def _distances(self, target: tuple[int, int]) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"BFS distance from every cell to ``target`` (cached per target).\"\"\"\n        cached = self._dist_cache.get(target)\n        if cached is not None:\n            return cached\n        dist = np.full(self.walls.shape, np.iinfo(np.int32).max // 2, dtype=np.int32)\n        dist[target] = 0\n        q: deque[tuple[int, int]] = deque([target])\n        while q:\n            y, x = q.popleft()\n            for dy, dx in ACTIONS:\n                ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx\n                if not self.walls[ny, nx] and dist[ny, nx] > dist[y, x] + 1:\n                    dist[ny, nx] = dist[y, x] + 1\n                    q.append((ny, nx))\n        self._dist_cache[target] = dist\n        return dist\n\n    def _obs(self) -> np.ndarray:\n        obs = np.zeros(self.observation_shape, dtype=np.float32)\n        obs[0] = self.walls\n        obs[1] = self.pellets\n        obs[2] = self.powers\n        obs[3][self.player] = 1.0\n        frightened = self.power_timer > 0\n        for g in self.ghosts:\n            if g.active:\n                obs[5 if frightened else 4][g.pos] = 1.0\n                obs[6][g.prev] = 1.0\n        if self.cfg.power_duration > 0:\n            obs[7] = self.power_timer / self.cfg.power_duration\n        return obs\n\n    def _info(self) -> dict:\n        return {\n            \"score\": self.score,\n            \"pellets_left\": self.pellets_left,\n            \"steps\": self.steps,\n     "input": {
      "description": "Dueling Q-network",
      "path": "/home/claude/pacdqn/pacdqn/model.py",
      "file_text": "\"\"\"Dueling Q-network for grid observations of shape (C, H, W).\n\nWorks on any spatial size (the flatten size is computed from ``obs_shape``),\nso the same network serves the small maze, the medium maze, or a downsampled\nAtari frame stack.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport torch\nfrom torch import nn\n\n\nclass QNetwork(nn.Module):\n    def __init__(self, obs_shape: tuple[int, int, int], n_actions: int, hidden: int = 256):\n        super().__init__()\n        c, h, w = obs_shape\n        self.features = nn.Sequential(\n            nn.Conv2d(c, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1),\n            nn.ReLU(),\n            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1),\n            nn.ReLU(),\n            nn.Conv2d(64, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1),\n            nn.ReLU(),\n            nn.Flatten(),\n        )\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            flat = self.features(torch.zeros(1, c, h, w)).shape[1]\n        self.value = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(flat, hidden), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(hidden, 1))\n        self.advantage = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(flat, hidden), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(hidden, n_actions))\n        self.n_actions = n_actions\n        self.obs_shape = tuple(obs_shape)\n\n    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\n        f = self.features(x)\n        v = self.value(f)\n        a = self.advantage(f)\n        return v + a - a.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)\n"
    },

      "file_text": "\"\"\"Uniform experience replay.\n\nObservations are quantised to ``uint8`` (values are in ``[0, 1]``) so a\n100k-transition buffer for the medium maze fits in ~550 MB instead of ~2.2 GB.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Batch:\n    obs: np.ndarray  # float32 (B, C, H, W)\n    actions: np.ndarray  # int64 (B,)\n    rewards: np.ndarray  # float32 (B,)\n    next_obs: np.ndarray  # float32 (B, C, H, W)\n    dones: np.ndarray  # float32 (B,)  1.0 if terminal (bootstrapping stops)\n\n\nclass ReplayBuffer:\n    def __init__(self, capacity: int, obs_shape: tuple[int, ...], seed: int | None = None):\n        if capacity <= 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"capacity must be positive\")\n        self.capacity = int(capacity)\n        self.obs = np.zeros((capacity, *obs_shape), dtype=np.uint8)\n        self.next_obs = np.zeros((capacity, *obs_shape), dtype=np.uint8)\n        self.actions = np.zeros(capacity, dtype=np.int64)\n        self.rewards = np.zeros(capacity, dtype=np.float32)\n        self.dones = np.zeros(capacity, dtype=np.float32)\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.size = 0\n        self._rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n\n    def __len__(self) -> int:\n        return self.size\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _encode(obs: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        return np.rint(np.clip(obs, 0.0, 1.0) * 255.0).astype(np.uint8)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _decode(obs: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        return obs.astype(np.float32) / 255.0\n\n    def add(self, obs: np.ndarray, action: int, reward: float, next_obs: np.ndarray, done: bool) -> None:\n        i = self.pos\n        self.obs[i] = self._encode(obs)\n        self.next_obs[i] = self._encode(next_obs)\n        self.actions[i] = action\n        self.rewards[i] = reward\n        self.dones[i] = float(done)\n        self.pos = (self.pos + 1) % self.capacity\n        self.size = min(self.size + 1, self.capacity)\n\n    def sample(self, batch_size: int) -> Batch:\n        if self.size == 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"cannot sample from an empty buffer\")\n        idx = self._rng.integers(0, self.size, size=batch_size)\n        return Batch(\n            obs=self._decode(self.obs[idx]),\n            actions=self.actions[idx],\n            rewards=self.rewards[idx],\n            next_obs=self._decode(self.next_obs[idx]),\n            dones=self.dones[idx],\n        )\n"
    },

      "description": "Double DQN agent",
      "path": "/home/claude/pacdqn/pacdqn/agent.py",
      "file_text": "\"\"\"Double DQN agent with a dueling network, Huber loss and a hard target update.\n\nThe agent is deliberately small and readable; the classic DQN pieces are all\nhere and labelled: replay buffer, \u03b5-greedy exploration, a frozen target network,\nand the Double-DQN target (online net picks the action, target net scores it).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import asdict, dataclass\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport torch\nfrom torch import nn\n\nfrom .model import QNetwork\nfrom .replay import Batch, ReplayBuffer\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass AgentConfig:\n    gamma: float = 0.99\n    lr: float = 2.5e-4\n    batch_size: int = 64\n    buffer_size: int = 50_000\n    learning_starts: int = 2_000\n    train_every: int = 1\n    target_update: int = 1_000  # env steps between hard target syncs\n    eps_start: float = 1.0\n    eps_end: float = 0.05\n    eps_decay_steps: int = 50_000\n    reward_scale: float = 0.01  # env points -> training reward\n    grad_clip: float = 10.0\n    hidden: int = 256\n\n\nclass DQNAgent:\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        obs_shape: tuple[int, int, int],\n        n_actions: int,\n        config: AgentConfig | None = None,\n        device: str | torch.device | None = None,\n        seed: int | None = None,\n    ):\n        self.cfg = config or AgentConfig()\n        self.obs_shape = tuple(obs_shape)\n        self.n_actions = int(n_actions)\n        self.device = torch.device(device or (\"cuda\" if torch.cuda.is_available() else \"cpu\"))\n        if seed is not None:\n            torch.manual_seed(seed)\n        self._rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n\n        self.online = QNetwork(self.obs_shape, self.n_actions, self.cfg.hidden).to(self.device)\n        self.target = QNetwork(self.obs_shape, self.n_actions, self.cfg.hidden).to(self.device)\n        self.sync_target()\n        self.target.eval()\n        for p in self.target.parameters():\n            p.requires_grad_(False)\n\n        self.optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.online.parameters(), lr=self.cfg.lr, eps=1.5e-4)\n        self.loss_fn = nn.SmoothL1Loss()\n        self.buffer = ReplayBuffer(self.cfg.buffer_size, self.obs_shape, seed=seed)\n        self.steps = 0  # environment steps observed\n        self.updates = 0  # gradient updates performed\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------ acting\n    def epsilon(self, step: int | None = None) -> float:\n        s = self.steps if step is None else step\n        frac = min(1.0, s / max(1, self.cfg.eps_decay_steps))\n        return self.cfg.eps_start + frac * (self.cfg.eps_end - self.cfg.eps_start)\n\n    @torch.no_grad()\n    def q_values(self, obs: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        x = torch.as_tensor(obs, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)\n        return self.online(x).squeeze(0).cpu().numpy()\n\n    def act(self, obs: np.ndarray, epsilon: float | None = None) -> int:\n        eps = self.epsilon() if epsilon is None else epsilon\n        if self._rng.random() < eps:\n            return int(self._rng.integers(self.n_actions))\n        return int(np.argmax(self.q_values(obs)))\n\n    # ----------------------------------------------------------- learning\n    def observe(self, obs, action, reward, next_obs, done) -> float | None:\n        \"\"\"Store a transition and (maybe) train. Returns the loss if a step was taken.\"\"\"\n        self.buffer.add(obs, action, reward * self.cfg.reward_scale, next_obs, done)\n        self.steps += 1\n        loss = None\n        if self.steps >= self.cfg.learning_starts and self.steps % self.cfg.train_every == 0:\n            loss = self.train_step(self.buffer.sample(self.cfg.batch_size))\n        if self.steps % self.cfg.target_update == 0:\n            self.sync_target()\n        return loss\n\n    def train_step(self, batch: Batch) -> float:\n        d = self.device\n        obs = torch.as_tensor(batch.obs, device=d)\n        actions = torch.as_tensor(batch.actions, device=d)\n        rewards = torch.as_tensor(batch.rewards, device=d)\n        next_obs = torch.as_tensor(batch.next_obs, device=d)\n        dones = torch.as_tensor(batch.dones, device=d)\n\n        q = self.online(obs).gather(1, actions.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1)\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            # Double DQN: online network chooses, target network evaluates.\n            next_actions = self.online(next_obs).argmax(dim=1, keepdim=True)\n            next_q = self.target(next_obs).gather(1, next_actions).squeeze(1)\n            target = rewards + self.cfg.gamma * (1.0 - dones) * next_q\n\n        loss = self.loss_fn(q, target)\n        self.optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)\n        loss.backward()\n        if self.cfg.grad_clip > 0:\n            nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(self.online.parameters(), self.cfg.grad_clip)\n        self.optimizer.step()\n        self.updates += 1\n        return float(loss.item())\n\n    def sync_target(self) -> None:\n        self.target.load_state_dict(self.online.state_dict())\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------- persistence\n    def save(self, path) -> None:\n        torch.save(\n            {\n                \"online\": self.online.state_dict(),\n                \"optimizer\": self.optimizer.state_dict(),\n                \"steps\": self.steps,\n                \"updates\": self.updates,\n                \"config\": asdict(self.cfg),\n                \"obs_shape\": self.obs_shape,\n                \"n_actions\": self.n_actions,\n            },\n            path,\n        )\n\n    @classmethod\n    def load(cls, path, device: str | None = None, seed: int | None = None) -> \"DQNAgent\":\n        ckpt = torch.load(path, map_location=\"cpu\", weights_only=False)\n        cfg = AgentConfig(**ckpt[\"config\"])\n        agent = cls(tuple(ckpt[\"obs_shape\"]), ckpt[\"n_actions\"], cfg, device=device, seed=seed)\n        agent.online.load_state_dict(ckpt[\"online\"])\n        agent.sync_target()\n        agent.optimizer.load_state_dict(ckpt[\"optimizer\"])\n        agent.steps = ckpt[\"steps\"]\n        agent.updates = ckpt[\"updates\"]\n        return agent\n"
    },

      "file_text": "\"\"\"Train a Double DQN agent on the maze environment.\n\n    python -m pacdqn.train --maze small --ghosts 1 --steps 150000 --out runs/small\n\nWrites to ``--out``:\n  config.json   full env + agent config\n  log.csv       one row per finished episode (step, return, score, won, eps, loss)\n  eval.csv      one row per evaluation (step, mean_return, mean_score, win_rate)\n  latest.pt     most recent checkpoint\n  best.pt       checkpoint with the best evaluation mean_score\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport csv\nimport json\nimport random\nimport time\nfrom dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field, fields\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport torch\n\nfrom .agent import AgentConfig, DQNAgent\nfrom .env import EnvConfig, MazeEnv\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass EvalResult:\n    mean_return: float\n    mean_score: float\n    win_rate: float\n    mean_steps: float\n\n\ndef evaluate(agent: DQNAgent, env_cfg: EnvConfig, episodes: int, seed: int, epsilon: float = 0.02) -> EvalResult:\n    env = MazeEnv(env_cfg)\n    returns, scores, wins, lengths = [], [], [], []\n    for ep in range(episodes):\n        obs, info = env.reset(seed=seed + ep)\n        ret, done = 0.0, False\n        while not done:\n            obs, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(agent.act(obs, epsilon=epsilon))\n            ret += r\n            done = term or trunc\n        returns.append(ret)\n        scores.append(info[\"score\"])\n        wins.append(float(info[\"won\"]))\n        lengths.append(info[\"steps\"])\n    return EvalResult(float(np.mean(returns)), float(np.mean(scores)), float(np.mean(wins)), float(np.mean(lengths)))\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass TrainConfig:\n    steps: int = 150_000\n    seed: int = 0\n    out: str = \"runs/default\"\n    device: str | None = None\n    eval_every: int = 10_000\n    eval_episodes: int = 10\n    log_every: int = 20  # print every N episodes\n    env: EnvConfig = field(default_factory=EnvConfig)\n    agent: AgentConfig = field(default_factory=AgentConfig)\n\n\ndef seed_everything(seed: int) -> None:\n    random.seed(seed)\n    np.random.seed(seed)\n    torch.manual_seed(seed)\n\n\ndef train(cfg: TrainConfig, quiet: bool = False) -> DQNAgent:\n    out = Path(cfg.out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    seed_everything(cfg.seed)\n\n    env = MazeEnv(cfg.env)\n    agent = DQNAgent(env.observation_shape, env.n_actions, cfg.agent, device=cfg.device, seed=cfg.seed)\n    (out / \"config.json\").write_text(json.dumps(asdict(cfg), indent=2))\n    if not quiet:\n        print(f\"device={agent.device}  maze={cfg.env.maze} {env.height}x{env.width}  ghosts={cfg.env.n_ghosts}  \"\n              f\"params={sum(p.numel() for p in agent.online.parameters()):,}\")\n\n    log_f = open(out / \"log.csv\", \"w\", newline=\"\")\n    log = csv.writer(log_f)\n    log.writerow([\"step\", \"episode\", \"return\", \"score\", \"won\", \"length\", \"epsilon\", \"loss\"])\n    eval_f = open(out / \"eval.csv\", \"w\", newline=\"\")\n    ev = csv.writer(eval_f)\n    ev.writerow([\"step\", \"mean_return\", \"mean_score\", \"win_rate\", \"mean_steps\"])\n\n    obs, _ = env.reset(seed=cfg.seed)\n    ep_return, ep_losses, episode = 0.0, [], 0\n    recent_returns: list[float] = []\n    best_score = -float(\"inf\")\n    t0 = time.time()\n    next_eval = cfg.eval_every\n\n    try:\n        for step in range(1, cfg.steps + 1):\n            action = agent.act(obs)\n            next_obs, reward, term, trunc, info = env.step(action)\n            # Only true terminals stop bootstrapping; time-limit truncation does not.\n            loss = agent.observe(obs, action, reward, next_obs, term)\n            if loss is not None:\n                ep_losses.append(loss)\n            ep_return += reward\n            obs = next_obs\n\n            if term or trunc:\n                episode += 1\n                mean_loss = float(np.mean(ep_losses)) if ep_losses else float(\"nan\")\n                log.writerow([step, episode, f\"{ep_return:.1f}\", f\"{info['score']:.0f}\", int(info[\"won\"]),\n                              info[\"steps\"], f\"{agent.epsilon():.3f}\", f\"{mean_loss:.5f}\"])\n                recent_returns.append(ep_return)\n                if not quiet and episode % cfg.log_every == 0:\n                    sps = step / max(1e-9, time.time() - t0)\n                    print(f\"step {step:>8,}  ep {episode:>5}  avg_return(last {cfg.log_every}) \"\n                          f\"{np.mean(recent_returns[-cfg.log_every:]):>8.1f}  eps {agent.epsilon():.3f}  \"\n                          f\"loss {mean_loss:.4f}  {sps:,.0f} steps/s\")\n                obs, _ = env.reset()\n                ep_return, ep_losses = 0.0, []\n\n            if step >= next_eval or step == cfg.steps:\n                next_eval += cfg.eval_every\n                res = evaluate(agent, cfg.env, cfg.eval_episodes, seed=10_000 + step)\n                ev.writerow([step, f\"{res.mean_return:.1f}\", f\"{res.mean_score:.1f}\", f\"{res.win_rate:.2f}\", f\"{res.mean_steps:.1f}\"])\n                eval_f.flush()\n                log_f.flush()\n                agent.save(out / \"latest.pt\")\n                if res.mean_score > best_score:\n                    best_score = res.mean_score\n                    agent.save(out / \"best.pt\")\n                if not quiet:\n                    print(f\"  [eval @ {step:,}] mean_score {res.mean_score:.1f}  win_rate {res.win_rate:.0%}  \"\n                          f\"mean_len {res.mean_steps:.0f}{'  *best*' if res.mean_score >= best_score else ''}\")\n    finally:\n        log_f.close()\n        eval_f.close()\n        agent.save(out / \"latest.pt\")\n    return agent\n\n\ndef _add_dataclass_args(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser, dc, prefix: str = \"\", skip=()) -> None:\n    for f in fields(dc):\n        if f.name in skip:\n            continue\n        default = f.default if f.default is not f.default_factory else None  # type: ignore[attr-defined]\n        if isinstance(default, (int, float, str)) and not isinstance(default, bool):\n            parser.add_argument(f\"--{prefix}{f.name.replace('_', '-')}\", type=type(default), default=default,\n                                help=f\"(default: {default})\")\n\n\ndef build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\n    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Train a Double DQN agent on a Pac-Man-style maze.\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--maze\", default=\"small\", help=\"small | medium\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--ghosts\", type=int, default=1)\n    p.add_argument(\"--lives\", type=int, default=1)\n    p.add_argument(\"--max-episode-steps\", type=int, default=500)\n    p.add_argument(\"--power-duration\", type=int, default=20)\n    p.add_argument(\"--steps\", type=int, default=150_000)\n    p.add_argument(\"--seed\", type=int, default=0)\n    p.add_argument(\"--out\", default=\"runs/default\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--device\", default=None, help=\"cpu | cuda (default: cuda if available)\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--eval-every\", type=int, default=10_000)\n    p.add_argument(\"--eval-episodes\", type=int, default=10)\n    p.add_argument(\"--quiet\", action=\"store_true\")\n    _add_dataclass_args(p, AgentConfig)\n    return p\n\n\ndef config_from_args(args: argparse.Namespace) -> TrainConfig:\n    agent_kwargs = {f.name: getattr(args, f.name) for f in fields(AgentConfig) if hasattr(args, f.name)}\n    env_cfg = EnvConfig(maze=args.maze, n_ghosts=args.ghosts, lives=args.lives,\n                        max_steps=args.max_episode_steps, power_duration=args.power_duration)\n    return TrainConfig(steps=args.steps, seed=args.seed, out=args.out, device=args.device,\n                       eval_every=args.eval_every, eval_episodes=args.eval_episodes,\n                       env=env_cfg, agent=AgentConfig(**agent_kwargs))\n\n\ndef main(argv=None) -> None:\n    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)\n    train(config_from_args(args), quiet=args.quiet)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"

= float(np.mean(ep_losses)) if ep_losses else float(\"nan\")\n                log.writerow([step, episode, f\"{ep_return:.1f}\", f\"{info['score']:.0f}\", int(info[\"won\"]),\n f\"{np.mean(recent_returns[-cfg.log_every:]):>8.1f}  eps {agent.epsilon():.3f}  \"\n                          f\"loss {mean_loss:.4f}  {sps:,.0f} steps/s\")\n                obs, _ = env.reset()\n                ep_return, ep_losses = 0.0, []\n\n            if step >= next_eval or step == cfg.steps:\n                next_eval += cfg.eval_every\n                res = evaluate(agent, cfg.env, eval_f.flush()\n                log_f.flush()\n                agent.save(out / \"latest.pt\")\n                if res.mean_score > best_score:\n                    best_score = res.mean_score\n                f\"mean_len {res.mean_steps:.0f}{'  *best*' if res.mean_score >= best_score else ''}\")\n    finally:\n        log_f.close()\n        eval_f.close()\n        agent.save(out /       "description": "Environment and maze tests",
      "path": "/home/claude/pacdqn/tests/test_env.py",
      "file_text": "import numpy as np\nimport pytest\n\nfrom pacdqn.env import ACTIONS, N_ACTIONS, NUM_CHANNELS, EnvConfig, MazeEnv\nfrom pacdqn.mazes import LAYOUTS, parse_layout, reachable_from\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------- mazes\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"name\", sorted(LAYOUTS))\ndef test_layouts_are_valid_and_connected(name):\n    lay = LAYOUTS[name]\n    seen = reachable_from(lay.walls, lay.player_start)\n    assert seen[lay.pellets | lay.powers].all()\n    for g in lay.ghost_starts:\n        assert seen[g]\n    assert not lay.walls[lay.player_start]\n    assert lay.n_pellets > 0\n\n\ndef test_parse_rejects_bad_layouts():\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=\"enclosed\"):\n        parse_layout(\"x\", \"#####\\n#P.G.\\n#####\")\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=\"no player\"):\n        parse_layout(\"x\", \"#####\\n#..G#\\n#####\")\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=\"no ghost\"):\n        parse_layout(\"x\", \"#####\\n#P..#\\n#####\")\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=\"unreachable\"):\n        parse_layout(\"x\", \"#######\\n#P.#.G#\\n#######\")\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=\"same width\"):\n        parse_layout(\"x\", \"#####\\n#P.G#\\n####\")\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=\"invalid char\"):\n        parse_layout(\"x\", \"#####\\n#PxG#\\n#####\")\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------- env\ndef test_reset_obs_shape_and_channels():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1))\n    obs, info = env.reset(seed=0)\n    assert obs.shape == (NUM_CHANNELS, env.height, env.width)\n    assert obs.dtype == np.float32\n    assert obs.min() >= 0.0 and obs.max() <= 1.0\n    assert obs[3].sum() == 1  # exactly one player\n    assert obs[4].sum() == 1  # one dangerous ghost\n    assert obs[5].sum() == 0  # no frightened ghosts\n    assert obs[7].max() == 0  # no power timer\n    assert info[\"pellets_left\"] == env.layout.n_pellets\n    assert np.array_equal(obs[0].astype(bool), env.walls)\n\n\ndef test_deterministic_given_seed():\n    def rollout(seed):\n        env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"medium\", n_ghosts=3))\n        env.reset(seed=seed)\n        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n        trace = []\n        done = False\n        while not done:\n            obs, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(rng.integers(N_ACTIONS))\n            trace.append((r, env.player, tuple(g.pos for g in env.ghosts)))\n            done = term or trunc\n        return trace\n\n    assert rollout(7) == rollout(7)\n    assert rollout(7) != rollout(8)\n\n\ndef test_cannot_walk_through_walls():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=0))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    # In the small maze the player starts at (9,6), walled left/right/below.\n    for a in (1, 2, 3):  # down, left, right\n        pos = env.player\n        env.step(a)\n        assert env.player == pos\n    env.step(0)  # up is open\n    assert env.player == (8, 6)\n\n\ndef test_pellets_reward_and_step_penalty():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=0))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    R = env.cfg.rewards\n    left_before = env.pellets_left\n    _, r, *_ = env.step(0)  # up onto a pellet\n    assert r == pytest.approx(R.pellet + R.step)\n    assert env.pellets_left == left_before - 1\n    _, r, *_ = env.step(1)  # back down to the (empty) start cell\n    assert r == pytest.approx(R.step)\n\n\ndef test_ghost_collision_ends_episode_with_death_penalty():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1, ghost_speed=0.0))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    # Teleport the ghost directly above the player, then step into it.\n    env.ghosts[0].pos = env.ghosts[0].prev = (8, 6)\n    obs, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(0)\n    assert term and not trunc\n    assert r == pytest.approx(env.cfg.rewards.death + env.cfg.rewards.pellet + env.cfg.rewards.step)\n    assert info[\"lives\"] == 0\n    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):\n        env.step(0)\n\n\ndef test_multiple_lives_respawn():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1, lives=2, ghost_speed=0.0))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    env.ghosts[0].pos = env.ghosts[0].prev = (8, 6)\n    _, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(0)\n    assert not term\n    assert info[\"lives\"] == 1\n    assert env.player == env.layout.player_start\n    assert env.ghosts[0].pos == env.ghosts[0].home\n\n\ndef test_power_pellet_makes_ghosts_edible():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1, ghost_speed=0.0, power_duration=5, ghost_respawn=3))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    # Move player next to the power pellet at (9,1): go to (9,2) via teleport.\n    env.player = (9, 2)\n    obs, r, *_ = env.step(2)  # left onto 'o'\n    assert env.power_timer > 0\n    assert obs[7].max() > 0\n    assert obs[5].sum() == 1 and obs[4].sum() == 0  # ghost now frightened in obs\n    # Put the frightened ghost in our path and eat it.\n    env.ghosts[0].pos = env.ghosts[0].prev = (9, 3)\n    obs, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(3)\n    assert not term\n    assert info[\"ghosts_eaten\"] == 1\n    assert r == pytest.approx(env.cfg.rewards.ghost + env.cfg.rewards.step)\n    assert not env.ghosts[0].active\n    assert obs[4].sum() == 0 and obs[5].sum() == 0  # off-board while respawning\n    for _ in range(3):\n        env.step(2)\n    assert env.ghosts[0].active and env.ghosts[0].pos == env.ghosts[0].home\n\n\ndef test_clearing_all_pellets_wins():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=0))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    env.pellets[:] = False\n    env.powers[:] = False\n    env.pellets[8, 6] = True  # one pellet directly above the player\n    obs, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(0)\n    assert term and info[\"won\"]\n    assert r == pytest.approx(env.cfg.rewards.pellet + env.cfg.rewards.clear + env.cfg.rewards.step)\n\n\ndef test_time_limit_truncates():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=0, max_steps=7))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    for i in range(7):\n        _, _, term, trunc, _ = env.step(1)  # bump into wall repeatedly\n    assert trunc and not term\n\n\ndef test_ghosts_chase_when_aggressive():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1, ghost_aggression=(1.0,)))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    d0 = env._distances(env.player)[env.ghosts[0].pos]\n    env.step(1)  # player bumps wall, stays put\n    d1 = env._distances(env.player)[env.ghosts[0].pos]\n    assert d1 == d0 - 1\n\n\ndef test_frightened_ghosts_flee():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1, ghost_aggression=(1.0,), frightened_speed=1.0, power_duration=50))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    env.power_timer = 50\n    env.ghosts[0].pos = env.ghosts[0].prev = (7, 6)  # open corridor\n    env.ghosts[0].direction = None\n    d0 = env._distances(env.player)[env.ghosts[0].pos]\n    env.step(1)\n    d1 = env._distances(env.player)[env.ghosts[0].pos]\n    assert d1 > d0\n\n\ndef test_legal_actions_and_render():\n    env = MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\"))\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    assert env.legal_actions() == [0]\n    text = env.render()\n    assert \"P\" in text and \"G\" in text and text.count(\"\\n\") == env.height\n\n\ndef test_invalid_config_and_action():\n    with pytest.raises(TypeError):\n        MazeEnv(nonsense=1)\n    with pytest.raises(KeyError):\n        MazeEnv(EnvConfig(maze=\"nope\"))\n    env = MazeEnv()\n    env.reset(seed=0)\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        env.step(9)\n\n\ndef test_gym_wrapper_if_available():\n    gym = pytest.importorskip(\"gymnasium\")\n    from pacdqn.env import make_gym_env\n\n    env = make_gym_env(EnvConfig(maze=\"small\"))\n    obs, info = env.reset(seed=0)\n    assert env.observation_space.contains(obs)\n    obs, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(env.action_space.sample())\n    assert env.observation_space.contains(obs)\n"
    },

      "file_text": "import csv\nimport json\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom pacdqn import play, train\nfrom pacdqn.agent import AgentConfig\nfrom pacdqn.env import EnvConfig\nfrom pacdqn.train import TrainConfig, evaluate\n\n\ndef test_train_smoke_writes_artifacts(tmp_path):\n    cfg = TrainConfig(\n        steps=300, seed=0, out=str(tmp_path / \"run\"), device=\"cpu\", eval_every=150, eval_episodes=2,\n        env=EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1, max_steps=40),\n        agent=AgentConfig(buffer_size=500, learning_starts=50, batch_size=8, target_update=50, hidden=32),\n    )\n    agent = train.train(cfg, quiet=True)\n    assert agent.steps == 300\n    run = tmp_path / \"run\"\n    assert (run / \"latest.pt\").exists() and (run / \"best.pt\").exists()\n    conf = json.loads((run / \"config.json\").read_text())\n    assert conf[\"env\"][\"maze\"] == \"small\" and conf[\"agent\"][\"hidden\"] == 32\n    with open(run / \"log.csv\") as f:\n        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))\n    assert len(rows) >= 300 // 40 - 1\n    assert all(float(r[\"epsilon\"]) <= 1.0 for r in rows)\n    with open(run / \"eval.csv\") as f:\n        ev = list(csv.DictReader(f))\n    assert [int(r[\"step\"]) for r in ev] == [150, 300]\n\n\ndef test_evaluate_returns_reasonable_stats():\n    cfg = EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1, max_steps=30)\n    agent = train.DQNAgent((8, 11, 13), 4, AgentConfig(hidden=16, buffer_size=10), device=\"cpu\", seed=0)\n    res = evaluate(agent, cfg, episodes=3, seed=0, epsilon=1.0)\n    assert 0.0 <= res.win_rate <= 1.0\n    assert 1 <= res.mean_steps <= 30\n    assert np.isfinite(res.mean_return) and np.isfinite(res.mean_score)\n\n\ndef test_cli_train_then_play_gif(tmp_path, capsys):\n    out = tmp_path / \"cli\"\n    train.main([\"--maze\", \"small\", \"--ghosts\", \"1\", \"--steps\", \"120\", \"--out\", str(out), \"--device\", \"cpu\",\n                \"--eval-every\", \"60\", \"--eval-episodes\", \"1\", \"--max-episode-steps\", \"30\",\n                \"--buffer-size\", \"300\", \"--learning-starts\", \"20\", \"--batch-size\", \"4\", \"--hidden\", \"16\", \"--quiet\"])\n    gif = tmp_path / \"play.gif\"\n    play.main([\"--run\", str(out), \"--episodes\", \"1\", \"--gif\", str(gif), \"--device\", \"cpu\"])\n    assert gif.exists() and gif.stat().st_size > 0\n    captured = capsys.readouterr().out\n    assert \"mean score\" in captured\n    play.main([\"--run\", str(out), \"--episodes\", \"1\", \"--random\", \"--delay\", \"-1\", \"--device\", \"cpu\"])\n    assert \"episode 1\" in capsys.readouterr().out\n"

      "code": "import csv\nimport json\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom pacdqn import play, train\nfrom pacdqn.agent import AgentConfig\nfrom pacdqn.env import EnvConfig\nfrom pacdqn.train import TrainConfig, evaluate\n\n\ndef test_train_smoke_writes_artifacts(tmp_path):\n    cfg = TrainConfig(\n        steps=300, seed=0, out=str(tmp_path / \"run\"), device=\"cpu\", eval_every=150, eval_episodes=2,\n        env=EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1, max_steps=40),\n        agent=AgentConfig(buffer_size=500, learning_starts=50, batch_size=8, target_update=50, hidden=32),\n    )\n    agent = train.train(cfg, quiet=True)\n    assert agent.steps == 300\n    run = tmp_path / \"run\"\n    assert (run / \"latest.pt\").exists() and (run / \"best.pt\").exists()\n    conf = json.loads((run / \"config.json\").read_text())\n    assert conf[\"env\"][\"maze\"] == \"small\" and conf[\"agent\"][\"hidden\"] == 32\n    with open(run / \"log.csv\") as f:\n        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))\n    assert len(rows) >= 300 // 40 - 1\n    assert all(float(r[\"epsilon\"]) <= 1.0 for r in rows)\n    with open(run / \"eval.csv\") as f:\n        ev = list(csv.DictReader(f))\n    assert [int(r[\"step\"]) for r in ev] == [150, 300]\n\n\ndef test_evaluate_returns_reasonable_stats():\n    cfg = EnvConfig(maze=\"small\", n_ghosts=1, max_steps=30)\n    agent = train.DQNAgent((8, 11, 13), 4, AgentConfig(hidden=16, buffer_size=10), device=\"cpu\", seed=0)\n    res = evaluate(agent, cfg, episodes=3, seed=0, epsilon=1.0)\n    assert 0.0 <= res.win_rate <= 1.0\n    assert 1 <= res.mean_steps <= 30\n    assert np.isfinite(res.mean_return) and np.isfinite(res.mean_score)\n\n\ndef test_cli_train_then_play_gif(tmp_path, capsys):\n    out = tmp_path / \"cli\"\n    train.main([\"--maze\", \"small\", \"--ghosts\", \"1\", \"--steps\", \"120\", \"--out\", str(out), \"--device\", \"cpu\",\n                \"--eval-every\", \"60\", \"--eval-episodes\", \"1\", \"--max-episode-steps\", \"30\",\n                \"--buffer-size\", \"300\", \"--learning-starts\", \"20\", \"--batch-size\", \"4\", \"--hidden\", \"16\", \"--quiet\"])\n    gif = tmp_path / \"play.gif\"\n    play.main([\"--run\", str(out), \"--episodes\", \"1\", \"--gif\", str(gif), \"--device\", \"cpu\"])\n    assert gif.exists() and gif.stat().st_size > 0\n    captured = capsys.readouterr().out\n    assert \"mean score\" in captured\n    play.main([\"--run\", str(out), \"--episodes\", \"1\", \"--random\", \"--delay\", \"-1\", \"--device\", \"cpu\"])\n    assert \"episode 1\" in capsys.readouterr().out\n",
      "filename": "/home/claude/pacdqn/tests/test_train_play.py"
    },

      "description": "Project README",
      "path": "/home/claude/pacdqn/README.md",
      "file_text": "# pacdqn \u2014 a Double DQN agent that learns a Pac-Man-style maze from scratch\n\nA complete, tested, dependency-light deep Q-learning project: an original\nPac-Man-style grid environment (pellets, power pellets, ghosts that chase and\nflee), a dueling Double-DQN agent in PyTorch, a training loop with evaluation\nand checkpoints, and a player that renders the agent in your terminal or to a GIF.\n\nThe agent starts knowing nothing and improves purely by playing \u2014 the opposite of\na pretrained decision model like Jev.\n\n```\npacdqn/\n  pacdqn/\n    mazes.py    maze layouts + parser/validator (BFS connectivity check)\n    env.py      MazeEnv \u2014 Gymnasium-style API, 8-channel grid observation\n    model.py    QNetwork \u2014 conv trunk + dueling value/advantage heads\n    replay.py   ReplayBuffer \u2014 uniform replay, uint8 storage\n    agent.py    DQNAgent \u2014 \u03b5-greedy, Double DQN target, Huber loss, hard target sync\n    train.py    CLI training loop, CSV logs, eval, best/latest checkpoints\n    play.py     watch a checkpoint in the terminal or record a GIF\n  tests/        31 pytest tests (env rules, replay, model, agent math, CLI smoke)\n  runs/small/   a finished demo run (config, logs, checkpoints, GIF)\n  run.bat       Windows: install deps, run tests, train, record GIF\n```\n\n## Quick start\n\n```bat\npip install -r requirements.txt\npython -m pytest -q                      # 31 tests, ~10 s on CPU\npython -m pacdqn.train --maze small --ghosts 1 --steps 150000 --out runs/small\npython -m pacdqn.play  --run runs/small  # watch it in the terminal\npython -m pacdqn.play  --run runs/small --gif runs/small/play.gif\n```\n\nOr on Windows just double-click `run.bat` (it does all of the above).\n\nIf you have an NVIDIA GPU, install the CUDA build of PyTorch first\n(`pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124`) \u2014 the\ntrainer auto-selects `cuda` when available and is ~10-30\u00d7 faster.\n\n## How the pieces fit \u2014 the DQN loop\n\n```\n                 \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510\n                 \u2502  for each env step:                                \u2502\n   obs \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u25ba\u2502  1. a = \u03b5-greedy(Q_online(obs))         agent.act  \u2502\n                 \u2502  2. obs', r, done = env.step(a)          env.step  \u2502\n                 \u2502  3. buffer.add(obs, a, r\u00b7scale, obs', done)        \u2502\n                 \u2502  4. every 4 steps: sample batch, one SGD step      \u2502\n                 \u2502        target = r + \u03b3\u00b7(1-done)\u00b7Q_target(s', a*)    \u2502\n                 \u2502                 where a* = argmax Q_online(s')     \u2502\n                 \u2502        loss = Huber(Q_online(s,a), target)         \u2502\n                 \u2502  5. every 1000 steps: Q_target \u2190 Q_online          \u2502\n                 \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518\n```\n\nEach idea and why it's there:\n\n| Piece | Why |\n|---|---|\n| **Replay buffer** | Breaks the correlation between consecutive frames; lets each transition be reused many times. |\n| **\u03b5-greedy, decayed** | Explore randomly at first (\u03b5=1), exploit later (\u03b5=0.05). Linear decay over `eps_decay_steps`. |\n| **Target network** | The regression target moves every update otherwise; a frozen copy makes training stable. |\n| **Double DQN** | Plain DQN's `max` overestimates Q. Choosing the action with the online net and *scoring* it with the target net removes most of that bias. |\n| **Dueling head** | Splits Q into V(s) + A(s,a). Learns \"this state is bad\" without needing to see every action from it. |\n| **Huber loss + grad clipping** | Large TD errors (dying = -5) don't blow up the gradient. |\n| **Reward scaling** | Env rewards are in game points (pellet 10, death -500). The agent trains on `points \u00d7 0.01`, keeping targets in a sane range. |\n| **Terminal vs. truncated** | Death stops bootstrapping; hitting the step limit does not (the state isn't actually terminal). |\n\n## The environment\n\nOriginal Pac-Man-style maze (no Namco assets). Legend in `mazes.py`; two layouts\nship (`small` 11\u00d713, `medium` 18\u00d719 with a 3-cell ghost house). Add your own by\nwriting a string \u2014 the parser validates that it's enclosed and every pellet is\nreachable.\n\n* **Actions** 0 up \u00b7 1 down \u00b7 2 left \u00b7 3 right. Walking into a wall = stay put.\n* **Ghosts** move every step (`ghost_speed`), can't reverse mid-corridor (like\n  the arcade), and each has an *aggression* \u2014 the probability it takes the\n  BFS-shortest step toward you instead of a random one. Ghost 1 is 0.9, ghost 2\n  is 0.7, \u2026 so more ghosts = more varied pressure.\n* **Power pellets** make ghosts flee (they maximise distance) at half speed for\n  `power_duration` steps; eating one sends it home for `ghost_respawn` steps.\n* **Rewards** (points): pellet +10, power +50, ghost +200, clear +500, death\n  -500, every step -1.\n* **Observation** `float32 (8, H, W)`: walls, pellets, power pellets, player,\n  dangerous ghosts, frightened ghosts, ghosts' previous cells (gives heading),\n  and a uniform channel with the power-timer fraction. It's Markov enough that\n  no frame stacking is needed.\n* `make_gym_env()` returns a proper `gymnasium.Env` if you have gymnasium\n  installed (for Stable-Baselines3 etc.). Not required.\n\n## Reading the results\n\n`train.py` writes `log.csv` (one row per episode) and `eval.csv` (every\n`--eval-every` steps, 10 greedy episodes with \u03b5=0.02). Quick plot:\n\n```python\nimport pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nev = pd.read_csv(\"runs/small/eval.csv\")\nev.plot(x=\"step\", y=[\"mean_score\", \"win_rate\"], subplots=True); plt.show()\n```\n\nA random policy on `small` with 1 ghost scores about **-490** (it dies almost\nimmediately). The included demo run shows what the agent does with a few minutes\nof CPU time \u2014 see `runs/small/eval.csv` and `runs/small/play.gif`.\n\n## Tuning knobs (all CLI flags)\n\n```\n--maze small|medium   --ghosts N   --lives N   --max-episode-steps N   --power-duration N\n--steps N             --eval-every N            --eval-episodes N       --seed N   --device cpu|cuda\n--gamma --lr --batch-size --buffer-size --learning-starts --train-every --target-update\n--eps-start --eps-end --eps-decay-steps --reward-scale --grad-clip --hidden\n```\n\nCurriculum that works: `small` + 1 ghost first (150k steps), then `medium` + 2\nghosts with `--eps-decay-steps 300000 --steps 1000000 --buffer-size 200000`.\n\n## Where to go next\n\n1. **Prioritized replay** \u2014 sample transitions with large TD error more often. `replay.py` is 60 lines; swap the uniform `sample` for a sum-tree.\n2. **n-step returns** \u2014 bootstrap from `r\u2081 + \u03b3r\u2082 + \u03b3\u00b2r\u2083 + \u03b3\u00b3Q(s\u2084)` instead of one step. Faster credit assignment for the delayed death penalty.\n3. **Noisy nets / distributional (C51)** \u2014 the rest of the Rainbow paper.\n4. **Real Atari Ms. Pac-Man** \u2014 `pip install \"gymnasium[atari]\"` (ale-py bundles the ROMs). Wrap frames to `(4, 84, 84)` with `gymnasium.wrappers.AtariPreprocessing` + `FrameStackObservation`; `QNetwork` already accepts any `(C, H, W)`, so the agent is unchanged. Expect ~10M frames on a GPU for good play.\n5. **Compare to a System-1 model** \u2014 feed `env.render()` to Jev each step and ask \"which direction?\" \u2014 no training, instant policy, no improvement. Same harness, opposite philosophy.\n\n## Reference\n\nMnih et al. 2015 (DQN) \u00b7 van Hasselt et al. 2016 (Double DQN) \u00b7 Wang et al. 2016 (Dueling) \u00b7 Hessel et al. 2018 (Rainbow).\n"
    },

Q_online          \u2502\n                 \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518\n```\n\nEach idea and why it's there:\n\n| Piece | Why |\n|---|---|\n| **Replay buffer** | Breaks the correlation between consecutive frames; lets each transition be reused many times. |\n| **\u03b5-greedy, decayed** | Explore randomly at first (\u03b5=1), exploit later (\u03b5=0.05). Linear decay over `eps_decay_steps`. |\n| **Target network** | The regression target moves every update otherwise; a frozen copy makes training stable. |\n| **Double DQN** | Plain DQN's `max` overestimates Q. Choosing the action with the online net and *scoring* it with the target net removes most of that bias. |\n| **Dueling head** | Splits Q into V(s) + A(s,a). Learns \"this state is bad\" without needing to see every action from it. |\n| **Huber loss + grad clipping** | Large TD errors (dying = -5) don't blow up the gradient. |\n| **Reward scaling** | Env rewards are in game points (pellet 10, death -500). The agent trains on `points \u00d7 0.01`, keeping targets in a sane range. |\n| **Terminal vs. truncated** | Death stops bootstrapping; hitting the step limit does not (the state isn't actually terminal). |\n\n## The environment\n\nOriginal Pac-Man-style maze (no Namco assets). Legend in `mazes.py`; two layouts\nship (`small` 11\u00d713, `medium` 18\u00d719 with a 3-cell ghost house). Add your own by\nwriting a string \u2014 the parser validates that it's enclosed and every pellet is\nreachable.\n\n* **Actions** 0 up \u00b7 1 down \u00b7 2 left \u00b7 3 right. Walking into a wall = stay put.\n* **Ghosts** move every step (`ghost_speed`), can't reverse mid-corridor (like\n  the arcade), and each has an *aggression* \u2014 the probability it takes the\n  BFS-shortest step toward you instead of a random one. Ghost 1 is 0.9, ghost 2\n  is 0.7, \u2026 so more ghosts = more varied pressure.\n* **Power pellets** make ghosts flee (they maximise distance) at half speed for\n  `power_duration` steps; eating one sends it home for `ghost_respawn` steps.\n* **Rewards** (points): pellet +10, power +50, ghost +200, clear +500, death\n  -500, every step -1.\n* **Observation** `float32 (8, H, W)`: walls, pellets, power pellets, player,\n  dangerous ghosts, frightened ghosts, ghosts' previous cells (gives heading),\n  and a uniform channel with the power-timer fraction. It's Markov enough that\n  no frame stacking is needed.\n* `make_gym_env()` returns a proper `gymnasium.Env` if you have gymnasium\n  installed (for Stable-Baselines3 etc.). Not required.\n\n## Reading the results\n\n`train.py` writes `log.csv` (one row per episode) and `eval.csv` (every\n`--eval-every` steps, 10 greedy episodes with \u03b5=0.02). Quick plot:\n\n```python\nimport pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nev = pd.read_csv(\"runs/small/eval.csv\")\nev.plot(x=\"step\", y=[\"mean_score\", \"win_rate\"], subplots=True); plt.show()\n```\n\nA random policy on `small` with 1 ghost scores about **-490** (it dies almost\nimmediately). The included demo run shows what the agent does with a few minutes\nof CPU time \u2014 see `runs/small/eval.csv` and `runs/small/play.gif`.\n\n## Tuning knobs (all CLI flags)\n\n```\n--maze small|medium   --ghosts N   --lives N   --max-episode-steps N   --power-duration N\n--steps N             --eval-every N            --eval-episodes N       --seed N   --device cpu|cuda\n--gamma --lr --batch-size --buffer-size --learning-starts --train-every --target-update\n--eps-start --eps-end --eps-decay-steps --reward-scale --grad-clip --hidden\n```\n\nCurriculum that works: `small` + 1 ghost first (150k steps), then `medium` + 2\nghosts with `--eps-decay-steps 300000 --steps 1000000 --buffer-size 200000`.\n\n## Where to go next\n\n1. **Prioritized replay** \u2014 sample transitions with large TD error more often. `replay.py` is 60 lines; swap the uniform `sample` for a sum-tree.\n2. **n-step returns** \u2014 bootstrap from `r\u2081 + \u03b3r\u2082 + \u03b3\u00b2r\u2083 + \u03b3\u00b3Q(s\u2084)` instead of one step. Faster credit assignment for the delayed death penalty.\n3. **Noisy nets / distributional (C51)** \u2014 the rest of the Rainbow paper.\n4. **Real Atari Ms. Pac-Man** \u2014 `pip install \"gymnasium[atari]\"` (ale-py bundles the ROMs). Wrap frames to `(4, 84, 84)` with `gymnasium.wrappers.AtariPreprocessing` + `FrameStackObservation`; `QNetwork` already accepts any `(C, H, W)`, so the agent is unchanged. Expect ~10M frames on a GPU for good play.\n5. **Compare to a System-1 model** \u2014 feed `env.render()` to Jev each step and ask \"which direction?\" \u2014 no training, instant policy, no improvement. Same harness, opposite philosophy.\n\n## Reference\n\nMnih et al. 2015 (DQN) \u00b7 van Hasselt et al. 2016 (Double DQN) \u00b7 Wang et al. 2016 (Dueling) \u00b7 Hessel et al. 2018 (Rainbow).\n",
      "filename": "/home/claude/pacdqn/README.md"
    },
